The Miscellaneous petition is filed by the petitioners under Section 263 R/w. Sec. 283 of Indian Succession Act seeking to set aside the order passed in P & S.C. No.247/2014 and consequently to revoke the succession certificate issued in favour of respondents No.1 and 2.

Case of the plaintiffs in O.S. No.5856/2013 in brief is as hereunder:-
C/w. Misc. No.437/2015
The plaintiffs are the children of defendant No.1.

Defendants No.2(a) to (c) are the legal heirs of Sri. Ramanjineya who is the son of defendant No.1 and defendants No.3(a) & (b) are the legal heirs of deceased K.R.Harish and defendant No.4 is the brother of the plaintiffs.

One Shivagange Ramaiah was the propositor of the family of the plaintiffs and defendants No.1 to 5 and he had 2 sons by name Hanumanthappa and Ramachandrappa and plaintiffs and defendants No.1 to 4 are the legal heirs of deceased Ramachandrappa.
It is stated that under the family partition between Hanumanthappa and Ramachandrappa dated 26.09.1956 various properties were allotted to the share of Ramachandrappa.
Ramakrishnappa inherited the ancestral properties from his father Ramachandrappa and also acquired various other properties out of joint nucleus of the ancestral properties.
Ramakrishnappa died on 15.03.1991 leaving behind the plaintiffs and defendants No.1 to 4 C/w. Misc. No.437/2015 as his legal successors.
After his demise, the plaintiffs and defendants continued to live as members of undivided Hindu joint family and are in joint possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule properties.

After the demise of Ramakrishnappa, the plaintiffs and defendants have sold few items of properties i.e. Sy. No.40/5 measuring 1 acre 10 guntas and Sy.
No.39/4 measuring 1 acre 23 guntas which stood in the name of their father Ramakrishnappa.
Further, the land bearing Sy. No.78/2 measuring 1 acre 7 guntas and Sy. No.9 measuring 24 guntas both situated at Doddakallasandra Village
were acquired by the Bank officers and Officials of House Building Society Ltd. and the defendant No.1 sold land in Sy. No.40/5 and Sy. No.36/5 to one K.Nagaraju under sale deed dated 23.08.1995.

It is stated that the first son of Ramakrishnappa namely Sri. Ramanjineya separated from family and was living separately and as such, Sri.
Harish was managing the entire affairs of the joint C/w. Misc. No.437/2015 family for and on behalf of other members of the joint family.
The plaintiffs were very young and pursuing their studies and had no worldly knowledge.

The deceased Harish was intelligent having worldly language and as such, the defendant No.1 used to hear the Shantha Kumar R vs Chandramma on 6 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162776421/
5 decision of Harish and accordingly, all the sale proceeds and compensation amount amounting to Rs.50,00,000/-

The said amount was deposited in the bank of defendants No.5 and 6.

The original FD receipts and other documents were held by deceased Harish who was acting as kartha of the family and after his demise the defendant No.3(a) being his wife was in possession of the original documents and she is now making hectic efforts to withdraw the amount by changing the nomination.
The defendant No.3(a) in collusion with the officials of defendants No.5 and 6 has changed the C/w. Misc. No.437/2015 nomination in her name.
During the life time of Harish he promised that the entire amount and interest will be utilized at proper time.
After his marriage he started living separately along with his wife and children and from past few years his health deteriorated and he died on 10.07.2013.
He had not used the fixed deposits amount for his personal gain.

But the plaintiffs learnt that the defendants No.3(a)

After coming to know of the illegal acts committed by the bank and defendant No.3(a), the plaintiffs immediately rushed to the bank and sought for necessary information, but the bank authorities failed to give any information and hence, the plaintiff issued legal notice calling upon the bank to not to meddle with the FD accounts.

The defendant No.2(a) has filed written statement wherein it is contended that the suit is frivolous, mischievous and is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and properties and hence, the suit is not maintainable and there is no cause of action to file the suit.

The relationship between the plaintiffs and defendants is admitted and the partition which took place between their ancestors Sri. Hanumanthappa and Sri. Ramachandrappa under partition deed dated C/w. Misc. No.437/2015 26.09.1956 is also admitted.

This defendant has also admitted the sale of some of the family properties and also admitted that the husband of this defendant Sri.

It is stated that without sharing the sale consideration he himself misused the huge fund and has deposited huge amount in the bank.

It is stated that the defendant No.3(a) and (b) have already enjoyed their share and the plaintiff and this defendant are entitled for the entire FD amount which is deposited in different branches and the defendant No.3(a) and (b) are not having any share in the FD amount.

sentences.text: Life Insurance Act, 1938 (4 of 1938) - Section 39 - Nominee's interest in the amount received under a policy when assured dying intestate - Held, subject to the claim of heirs of the assured under law of succession.

Held: 
A mere nomination made under Section 39 of the Act does not have the effect of conferring on the nominee any beneficial interest in the amount payable under the life insurance policy on the death of the assured.
The nomination only indicates the hand which is authorised to receive the amount, on the payment of which the insurer gets a valid discharge of its liability under the policy. Under Section 39

the policy-holder continues C/w. Misc. No.437/2015 to hold interest in the policy during his lifetime and the nominee acquires no sort of interest in the policy during the lifetime of the policy- holder.
Therefore, on the death of the policy- holder the amount payable under the policy becomes part of his estate which is governed by the law of succession applicable to him.
Such succession may be testamentary or intestate.
Section 39 does not operate as a third kind of succession which can be styled as a 'statutory testament'.
A nominee cannot be treated as being equivalent to an heir or legatee.
The amount received under the policy therefore, can be claimed by the heirs of the assured in accordance with the law of succession governing them.

The Miscellaneous petition is filed by the petitioners under Section 263 R/w. Sec. 283 of Indian Succession Act seeking to set aside the order passed in P & S.C. No.247/2014 and consequently to revoke the succession certificate issued in favour of respondents No.1 and 2.
2.
Ramakrishnappa inherited the ancestral properties from his father Ramachandrappa and also acquired various other properties out of joint nucleus of the ancestral properties.
Ramakrishnappa died on 15.03.1991 leaving behind the plaintiffs and defendants No.1 to 4 C/w. Misc. No.437/2015 as his legal successors.
After his demise, the plaintiffs and defendants continued to live as members of undivided Hindu joint family and are in joint possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule properties.
After his marriage he started living separately along with his wife and children and from past few years his health deteriorated and he died on 10.07.2013.
After coming to know of the illegal acts committed by the bank and defendant No.3(a), the plaintiffs immediately rushed to the bank and sought for necessary information, but the bank authorities failed to give any information and hence, the plaintiff issued legal notice calling upon the bank to not to meddle with the FD accounts.
The defendant No.1 died during the pendency of the suit and she has not filed any written statement.
Since, the defendant No.3 had love and affection towards the plaintiffs No.2,
initially he nominated him in the fixed deposit and after he got married the defendant No.3(a) and defendant No.3(b) was born, he changed the nomination and thus, item No.7 of the suit properties C/w. Misc. No.437/2015 was the separate independent exclusive property of deceased Harish till his death and upon his demise these defendants have succeeded and inherited the same.
These respondents separated from joint family in the year 1996 itself and are residing separately and hence, the question of claiming the deposit amount in the name of these respondents by the appellants does not arise, since the documents clearly shows the nominees are respondents No.1 and 2 and both are entitled to the amount deposited in the fixed deposit, the petitioners have no right to question the order passed by this Court and thus, contending these facts sought for dismissal of petition.
Harish and therefore, the certificate issued was not defective and none of the petitioners herein are entitled to any share in respect of the deposits and hence, the certificate cannot be revoked and sought for dismissal of petition.
The succession certificate does not conclusively determine the rights of the parties in the matter of disputes between the parties.
This makes it clear that grantee of the succession certificate only gets C/w. Misc. No.437/2015 the power to sue for an action for recovery of money by following due process of law.
Therefore, the succession certificate granted in favour of respondents No.1 and 2 deserves to be set aside and consequently, it has to be revoked as sought by the petitioners.
